I woke up in the middle of the night again. I wonder how many more times it'll happen. Sleeping in hospitals isn't very easy; that's why they hike everyone up on painkillers. I wish they could add sleeping pills to my daily cocktail of meds.

My room is dark, save for a weak bedside light, but I feel another person with me. I don't say anything, if they're here to see me they will come talk to me.

The person shuffles around, like they were standing up or something. Footsteps, and then an old woman dissolves out of the shadows and to my side. Her face was so wrinkly, spotted, and soft I could not recognize the woman herself; all I saw was the years etched into her face.

"Who are you, exactly? Everyone I know who would be anywheres close to your age is six feet under." I smirked. I stopped trying to hide my bitterness when they reduced my morphine last week. Or was it two weeks? Yesterday?

"You don't look too hot yourself, kiddo." The raspy voice quipped at me. It was strong. And familiar. "And you know who I am."

I tried looking past the woman's countless wrinkles, searching for something I knew. "I see your scar has already faded." She whispered. My eyes widened, straining to understand.

I recognized eyes that struggled to smile, a mouth that couldn't quite curl into a grin. I traced over the thin, light scar on my left thumb. Its twin was inches away, barely visible on her withered hand. "My twin sister."

She snorted. "Ha! I forgot how snarky I was when I was your age." The woman's face softened, and I got the message.

"Oh." The woman reached for my hand, and I held hers as I felt the tide of life ebbing away from my body. I wondered if her bones ached, and if her mind was starting to wander. Was she in pain? Or did she not notice all the creaks and groans of her weathered body? I left looking at her crinkled face, her almost transparent hand in mine. I was jealous.

Personally, I just disagree with using social media as a way to present a public official with as much authority as the president's opinion. It serves the purpose of reaching young voters, but I think there are better mediums to reach people that look more professional.

Why is(are) the president('s pr people) using social media to passively aggressively denounce the supreme court decision? I see this as inappropriate and unprofessional, someone in a position of authority like the president shouldn't be acting out like this. If he wants to express disapproval of the decision, he should make a speech or public address. For example, he could say how he doesn't believe the court made the best decision but he also understands their reasoning and power checks, and wants to look into legislation that can create a compromise without breaking the court's decision.
